model_annotations.Bulgarian:
Figure 6 presents six subplots arranged in two columns and three rows, comparing the phenomena of massive activations and attention sinks across different gating configurations in neural network layers. The left column plots “Max Activation Value” against “Layer,” while the right column plots “first token attention scores” against “layer.” All plots share the same x-axis range from 0 to 20, representing layer indices. The left column uses a linear scale for the y-axis, while the right column uses a linear scale for the y-axis ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

The top-left subplot (“Massive Activation of baseline”) shows Max Activation Value (y-axis) versus Layer (x-axis). The y-axis ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200. Three lines are plotted: a solid blue line (“ attn_output”), a dashed red line (“ fm_output”), and a dash-dotted green line (“ attn_residual”). The blue line rises sharply after layer 5, peaks near layer 6 at approximately 1400, and then drops to near zero after layer 10. The red line follows a similar pattern but peaks slightly lower. The green line remains near zero until layer 10, then rises sharply to about 1000 before dropping again.

The top-right subplot (“first token attention scores of baseline”) plots first token attention scores (y-axis ranging from 0.0 to 1.0) against layer (x-axis from 0 to 20). The y-axis has tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The solid blue line (“first token attention score”) starts near 0.0, rises to approximately 0.8 at layer 5, fluctuates between 0.6 and 0.8 until layer 15, then rises to about 1.0 at layer 20. A horizontal dashed green line at 0.467 indicates the mean.

The middle-left subplot (“Massive Activation of y elementwise”) plots Max Activation Value (y-axis from 0 to 400, with tick marks at intervals of 50) against Layer (x-axis from 0 to 20). Three lines are plotted: solid blue (“ attn_output”), dashed red (“ fm_output”), and dash-dotted green (“ fm_residual”). The blue line remains near zero until layer 10, then rises sharply to approximately 350. The red line follows a similar pattern but peaks slightly higher. The green line remains near zero until layer 15, then rises sharply to approximately 350.

The middle-right subplot (“first token attention score of y elementwise”) plots first token attention scores (y-axis from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2) against layer (x-axis from 0 to 20). The solid blue line (“first token attention score”) starts near 0.0, rises to approximately 0.6 at layer 5, fluctuates between 0.4 and 0.6 until layer 15, then drops to approximately 0.2 at layer 20. A horizontal dashed green line at 0.268 indicates the mean.

The bottom-left subplot (“Massive Activation of attn output_gate_head_share”) plots Max Activation Value (y-axis from 0 to 500, with tick marks at intervals of 100) against Layer (x-axis from 0 to 20). Three lines are plotted: solid blue (“ attn_output”), dashed red (“ fm_output”), and dash-dotted green (“ attn_residual”). The blue line rises sharply after layer 5, peaks near layer 6 at approximately 400, then drops to near zero after layer 10. The red line follows a similar pattern but peaks slightly lower. The green line remains near zero until layer 10, then rises sharply to about 400 before dropping again.

The bottom-right subplot (“first token attention scores of attn output_gate_wo_sparisty”) plots first token attention scores (y-axis from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2) against layer (x-axis from 0 to 20). The solid blue line (“first token attention score”) starts near 0.0, rises to approximately 0.6 at layer 5, fluctuates between 0.4 and 0.6 until layer 15, then drops to approximately 0.2 at layer 20. A horizontal dashed green line at 0.461 indicates the mean.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations within a neural network architecture. The figure is organized into five rows, each displaying two charts: a left chart showing the maximum activation value across layers for a specific gating configuration, and a right chart showing the first token attention score across layers for the same configuration. The x-axis in all charts is labeled "Layer" and spans from 0 to 20, with numerical tick marks at regular intervals of 5. The y-axis in the left charts is labeled "Max Activation Value" and ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200. The y-axis in the right charts is labeled "first token attention score" and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Each chart in the left column plots three lines: a dashed blue line for "atten_output", a dashed red line for "fm_output", and a dashed green line for "fm_residual", all with circular markers. Each chart in the right column plots a single solid blue line for "first token attention score", with circular markers, and includes a horizontal dashed green line indicating the mean attention score for that configuration. Row 1, labeled "Baseline", shows significant massive activations and attention sinks emerging after the 6th layer, with the left chart displaying peaks exceeding 1400 and the right chart showing attention scores fluctuating around 0.467. Row 2, labeled "SDPA Gating", shows reduced activations and no attention sinks, with the left chart displaying activations below 350 and the right chart showing attention scores fluctuating around 0.248. Row 3, labeled "Value Layer Gating", shows similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks, with the left chart displaying activations below 350 and the right chart showing attention scores fluctuating around 0.297. Rows 4-5, labeled "Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid", show massive activations and attention sinks resembling the baseline, with the left chart displaying peaks exceeding 1400 and the right chart showing attention scores fluctuating around 0.461.
model_annotations.English: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in a neural network, with each row displaying distinct configurations and their corresponding behaviors across 21 layers. The left column plots show the maximum activation value (y-axis) for various gating components—'atten_output', 'atten_residual', 'fm_output', and 'fm_residual'—against the layer index (x-axis, ranging from 0 to 21). The right column plots show the first token attention score (y-axis) for the same components against the layer index (x-axis, ranging from 0 to 21). In Row 1 (Baseline), the left plot shows a sharp rise in activation values starting around layer 6, with 'atten_output' reaching approximately 1400 and 'fm_output' reaching approximately 1600 by layer 21. The right plot shows the first token attention score for 'atten_output' fluctuating between 0.0 and 0.8, with a mean of 0.467. In Row 2 (SDPA Gating), the left plot shows a similar activation pattern but with reduced activations and no attention sinks, while the right plot shows a lower mean attention score of 0.468. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid) show activation patterns resembling the baseline, with 'atten_output' reaching approximately 1400 and 'fm_output' reaching approximately 1600 by layer 21, while the attention scores show a mean of 0.461 and 0.361 respectively.
model_annotations.German: Figure 6 presents a comparative analysis of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations in neural network layers. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 and is marked with regular integer intervals, representing the layer index. The y-axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” is scaled linearly and ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at regular intervals of 200, indicating the maximum activation value observed in each layer. The first row displays three lines: a solid red line labeled “attn_output” starting near 0, rising sharply to a peak of approximately 1400 at layer 6, then dropping to near 0 by layer 10 before rising again to about 1200 at layer 20; a dashed green line labeled “attn_residual” that remains near 0 until layer 6, then spikes to approximately 1200, and stays near that level until layer 15 before declining; and a dotted blue line labeled “fm_output” that remains near 0 until layer 6, then rises to about 1000, and stays near that level until layer 15 before declining. The corresponding attention score plot for the baseline shows a solid blue line labeled “first token attention score” with a mean of 0.467, fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8 across layers 0 to 20. The second row shows similar patterns for the “atten_gate” configuration, with the solid red line “attn_output” peaking at approximately 350 at layer 6, then rising to about 380 at layer 20; the dashed green line “attn_residual” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to approximately 300, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining; and the dotted blue line “fm_output” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to about 250, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining. The corresponding attention score plot for “atten_gate” shows a solid blue line labeled “first token attention score” with a mean of 0.648, fluctuating between approximately 0.4 and 0.8 across layers 0 to 20. The third row shows similar patterns for the “v_elementwise” configuration, with the solid red line “attn_output” peaking at approximately 350 at layer 6, then rising to about 380 at layer 20; the dashed green line “attn_residual” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to approximately 300, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining; and the dotted blue line “fm_output” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to about 250, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining. The corresponding attention score plot for “v_elementwise” shows a solid blue line labeled “first token attention score” with a mean of 0.297, fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.4 across layers 0 to 20. The fourth row shows similar patterns for the “atten_output_gate_head_share” configuration, with the solid red line “attn_output” peaking at approximately 500 at layer 6, then declining to near 0 by layer 10 before rising again to about 400 at layer 20; the dashed green line “attn_residual” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to approximately 400, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining; and the dotted blue line “fm_output” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to about 300, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining. The corresponding attention score plot for “atten_output_gate_head_share” shows a solid blue line labeled “first token attention score” with a mean of 0.361, fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.5 across layers 0 to 20. The fifth row shows similar patterns for the “atten_output_gate_wo_sparcity” configuration, with the solid red line “attn_output” peaking at approximately 1400 at layer 6, then declining to near 0 by layer 10 before rising again to about 1200 at layer 20; the dashed green line “attn_residual” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to approximately 1200, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining; and the dotted blue line “fm_output” remaining near 0 until layer 6, then rising to about 1000, and staying near that level until layer 15 before declining. The corresponding attention score plot for “atten_output_gate_wo_sparcity” shows a solid blue line labeled “first token attention score” with a mean of 0.481, fluctuating between approximately 0.2 and 0.8 across layers 0 to 20.
